December 13, 2.

Dear Saint Oyant,

I forward herewith for your information tabulated
statements relating to three prisoners named Woo Lan Ding
(吳蘭亭) alias Woo Ts Tsung (吳士貞), Tseu Tong Hai
(周通海) and Tsoong Chiu Lien (鍾秋蓮) alias Tseong Lien
(鍾廉), who were arrested by Settlement Police at about
9 p.m. on October 25, 1932, outside the Doong Loh Teashop,
1877 Ying Hwa Li, Robison Road, where, prior to the arrival
of the Police, they had been holding a communist meeting.

The three accused appeared on remand before the 2nd
Branch Kiangsu High Court on December 9, when they were
ordered to be handed over to the Chinese Authorities.

Attached are lists of the communist literature seized
at the homes of the 1st and 3rd accused.

Yours sincerely,

Sub '¾
JJS

Inspector E. Saint Oyant,
Chief of the Political Section,
Shanghai Police Headquarters.

Mr. Lea appeared for the police.
Mr. Tseu Kyl Vung appeared for the I.S. Bureau.

Mr. Tseu:-These accused were implicated by others already in the custody of the I.S. Bureau. They do not want to reveal the names of those who implicated them, as they want to keep them secret, because they are expecting to affect another arrest.
Judge:-This Court has received no official document from the S.P. S. Bureau.

Mr. Lea :-Since the S.P.S. Bureau have not filed the official documents, I ask the Court to remand the case till next Wednesday.

Proceedings.
MR. ......... appeared for the police.
MR. KUO:- At ......... on the 23/1/32 the Detectives from the
......... Public Security Bureau came to the station and requested
a distance in arresting some communists in a tea shop at 1077
Ying Hwa Li off Robinson Road. When the police arrived at this
address the meeting had finished and the three accused were arrested
outside the tea shop. Later the police went to the house of the
1st accused at 3042 Ying Hwa Li off Robinson Rd and there they
found many copies of the 'Tsen Hwa' the meaning of this being
'True Force' and also 9 copies of the 'Hung Pao' in the same room;
These papers are all communistic. In the house of the 2nd accused
( a mud hut on the Macao Rd ) the police found nothing. At the house
of the 3rd accused No. 7 Foo Sung Li Chantu Rd in his room many
Communistic books were found. In the room of the 3rd accused the
police found a letter addressed to the accused in which his friend
told him that he had been released on security. ( Letter handed to
the Court. ) The 2nd accused was arrested by the Police of the
Settlement on the 2/9/32 and was then handed over to the Chinese
Authorities. The representative of the Bureau is now in Court
to ask that these accused be handed over but he has no Dispatch
for them. I ask that the case be remanded for the Bureau to
produce evidence against them.
C.D.C. 285:- At about 9.p.m on the 23rd inst the rep: of the
S.S.D. Bureau came to the station and asked for assistance to
arrest some Communists. Later the accused were brought to the
station. I found inflammatory literature in the rooms of the

1st accused: In reply to the Judge:- I met the 2nd
and the 3rd accused. I met the 2nd accused 3 days ago on the
road when it was then that we arranged to have a talk in the

2nd accused:- On the 2/9/31 I was arrested in landao

there was no meeting at this tea shop. I was there to talk business.
I do not know the 3rd accused but he did sit with us at the same
table.

3rd accused:- I met the 1st accused several days ago &
he asked me to meet him at this tea shop yesterday. When I arrived
the 1st and 2nd accused were there.

Witness Mr. Shing :- I represent the S.P.S. Bureau:-
Acting on information to the effect that a Communistic meeting was
to be held at this tea shop yesterday I went with others of the
Bureau to the Soctoo Road police station to get assistance for the
arrest of these accused. I have not the Dispatch with me now.
I will produce it at the next hearing.

Mr. Foo:- As the accused were all arrested in the
settlement if the Bureau wish that they be handed over their repres-
entative must first produce evidence to prove that they have been
concerned in any offence in Chinese territory.

Decision.    All accused to be detained in custody.

Extract of Daily Intelligence Report dated 24.10.32

Communist Propaganda - three arrests

At 8.50 p.m. October 23, acting on information received
from the Chinese Authorities to the effect that a meeting was
being held by six communist suspects in the Doon; Loh (同樂)
Teashop, No.1877 Ying Hwa Li, Robison Road, the Municipal
Police visited the teashop but found that the gathering
had already dispersed. However, the following three persons
reported to have been present at the meeting were subsequently
arrested on Robison Road outside the teashop :-

1. Woo Lan Ding (吳蘭亭), alias Woo Ts Tsung (吳子宗),
age 32, Hupeh, living at No.3442 Robison Road.

2. Tseu Tong Hai (周通海), age 21, Kempo, living in a
straw hut off Macao Road.

3. Tsong Chiu Yien (鐘秋炎), alias Tsong Lien(鐘廉),
age 25, Hunan, living at No.7 South Chengtu Road.

A search of the dwellings of the 1st and 3rd accused
resulted in the seizure of a quantity of communist and
pro-communist literature in Chinese and Japanese, but nothing
was found at the home of the 2nd accused. The accused will
be brought before Court on October 24 when an application
for their extradition to the Chinese Authorities will be
made.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsoong Chiu Yien.
native of Hunan taken by me C.D.3.283.
at P.Rd.Station. on the 23.10.32. and interpreted by Chang Wen Ta.

My name is Tsoong Chiu Yien, alias Tsoong Lien, I am native of
Dau Yuan Hsien of Hunan Province, unemployed, and living in a
room above the kitchen, No.7 Foo Zung Lee Alleyway, off Chengtu
Road. I am employed by the Chung Hwa Printing Works, Pakhoi Road,
as a coolie. At 7 p.m. to-day I went to the Doong Loh Teashop
Robison Road for the purpose of visiting my friend Woo Lan Ding
whom I knew since 3 or 4 years ago at Hankow. A few days ago
when I was on the way to the Orpheum Theatre, I met Woo Lan Ding
on the Robison Road, where he asked me to meet him to-day at the
Doong Loh Teashop as he requested me to get him a job. Half an
hour after I had talked with Woo Lan Ding, I was arrested by the
Police at the downstairs of the teashop. I don't known the
another man arrested by the Police.

Signed by Tsoong Chiu Yien.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Woo Lan Ding ,
native of Hupeh, taken by me O.D.3.283,
at 2nd. Station on the 23.10.32 and interpreted by Chang Wen Ta.

My name is Woo Lan Ding, alias Woo Ts Tsung, aged 32, I am a
native of Hupeh (Kiang Ling Hsien), married and living at 3442
Iung Hwa Li, Robison Road. At 7.30 p.m. on the 23.10.32 (to-day)
I went to the Doong Loh Teashop in the Iung Hwa Li Alleyway to
meet my friend Tsoong Lien, whom I requested to get me a job.
Tsoong Lien is working in the Chung Hwa Printing Co. at present,
whom I knew since 3 or 4 years ago at Hankow. A few days ago I
met Tsoong Lien on Robison Road where I asked him to meet in the
above teashop in this evening. When I arrived at the teashop
I Met Tsoong Lien and Lu Tong Hai, the latter consulted with
me about to carry out some hacker business. A while later when
we were stepping downstairs, we were arrested by the Police. The
above statement which I made is true.

Signed by Woo Lan Ding.
Witness C.D.C.170.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tsou Tong Hai,
native of Kompo, taken by me C.D.9.283.
at P.Rd. Station the 23.10.39. and interpreted by Chang Won Ta.

My name is Tsou Tong Hai, aged 21, I am a native of Kompo, employed at a building contractor's yard, Chapui, as a coolie and living in a straw hut on Macao Road. About 2 years ago I worked in the Doong Shing Cotton Mill together with Woo Lan Ding, since then I knew him. As Woo Lan Ding is out of work now, he requested me to do hawker business in company with him, but I think that he is not phisical strong enough to carry such a business. Learning that I have been planting vegetables, Woo Lan Ding asked me to meet him in the Doong Loh Teashop to discuss the vegetable business. At 8 p.m. today I went to the above teeshop to consulted with him about the hawker business, but I was arrested by the Police when I was stepping downstairs. I don't know anyone else. The above statement which I made is true.

Signed by Tsou Tong Hai.
